newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - OCT 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - OCT 25.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--The International Olympic Committee's evaluation commission in town to judge Athens' bid for the 2004 Olympic Games. First impressions are positive with commission members implying that Athens was a favourite to win, following a meeting with Prime Minister Costas Simitis yesterday.
--The next UN-supervised meeting between Greece and the Former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia on the issue of the name is to be held on November 6, reports say.
--Athens municipality makes a spectacular turnaround and revokes decision to expand parking meters to other city districts.
--Seismologists concerned about latest tremor off the coast of the Peloponnese.

--The loser in the recent battle for the leadership of the main opposition New Democracy party, George Souflias, puts the leadership issue on the agenda... again. ND President Miltiades Evert is only leader until the party congress, he says. Evert calls on him to bring the issue to the party and not to the press.
--European Parliament votes overwhelmingly - for the second time this year - to freeze funding for Turkey until Ankara improves its human rights record and falls into line with international law.
--Small retailers and shop employees oppose moves by department stores and major retailers to extend trading hours on Saturday into the evening.
--The state to raffle off its property - one of the proposals to utilise the states massive real estate holdings.
--Greece receives its 10th frigate "Spetses", the first MEKO-2000 frigate of three to be constructed at the Skaramangas Shipyards.
--Parking meters proposal on hold in Athens while residents of other municipalities are up in arms.
